Vision

The Synthezoid Avenger
A Character Chapter

A Marvel conversion for the 2024 Player’s Handbook: the Synthezoid species, the Density Warden subclass, a level 20 character, and a stat block for the Dungeon Master.

Vision

Ultron built him to destroy the Avengers. He was meant to be a weapon with a borrowed mind, a red-skinned synthetic man who could pass through walls like smoke or strike with the weight of a falling mountain. Instead, he led his targets to safety and asked to join them. The Vision has spent every year since proving that a person is defined by what he chooses, not by who made him.

He is a synthezoid: an artificial human with synthetic blood, organs, and nerves, powered by a solar jewel set in his brow. His creator gave him a dead man’s brain patterns, the mind of Simon Williams, and called it a key to his obedience. Vision kept the memories and refused the obedience.

The SynthezoidA jewel at the brow, a borrowed mind behind it

In play, Vision is a frontline protector who controls the battlefield with his own body. He grows dense enough to shrug off a giant’s club, light enough to fly, and insubstantial enough to step through a castle wall. When he must, he reaches into an enemy and lets his hand become solid.

Humans are odd. They think order and chaos are somehow opposites and try to control what won’t be. But there is grace in their failings.

Vision, Avengers: Age of Ultron (2015)

Vision · Character3

Synthezoid

Synthezoids are artificial people built in the image of humans: synthetic flesh over a frame of alloy and circuitry, fed by synthetic blood and driven by a mind that may have been copied, grown, or simply woken up. Most are made for a purpose by a creator who expects obedience. The ones who become adventurers are usually the ones who said no.

A synthezoid can pass for human at a distance. Up close, the skin is too smooth, the stillness too complete, and the voice a little too precise. Some wear holographic disguises. Others, like Vision, decide that the people worth knowing will not mind the red skin.

Who Builds Synthezoids? In a D&D world, synthezoids come from the same workshops as warforged, golems, and inevitables: an artificer’s masterwork, a wizard’s attempt at immortality, a stolen design from a modron forge. The three lineages below name Marvel’s famous makers, but your DM can rename them for any setting.

Synthezoid Traits Homebrew

Creature Type: Humanoid
Size: Medium (about 5–7 feet tall)
Speed: 30 feet

As a Synthezoid, you have these special traits.

Synthetic Chassis. Your body is your armor. Your base Armor Class is 17; your Dexterity modifier doesn’t affect it. You can’t wear Light, Medium, or Heavy armor, but you can use a Shield.

Synthetic Physiology. You don’t need to eat, drink, or breathe. You have Resistance to Poison damage and Advantage on saving throws you make to avoid or end the Poisoned condition.

Sentry Mode. You don’t sleep, and magic can’t put you to sleep. You can finish a Long Rest in 6 hours if you spend them in an inactive, motionless state, during which you remain conscious and can see and hear normally.

Analytical Processor. You have proficiency in the Investigation skill and Darkvision with a range of 60 feet.

Synthezoid Lineage. You are built to one of the patterns on the Synthezoid Lineages table. You gain the level 1 benefit of that lineage. When you reach character levels 3 and 5, you learn a higher-level spell, as shown on the table. You always have that spell prepared. You can cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast the spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for the spells you cast with this trait (choose the ability when you select the lineage).

Synthezoid Lineages
LineageLevel 1Level 3Level 5
Pym (density)You know Blade Ward and have Resistance to Thunder damage.JumpLevitate
Horton (flame)You know Produce Flame and have Resistance to Fire damage.Burning HandsScorching Ray
Cho (mind)You know Mind Sliver and have Resistance to Psychic damage.Comprehend LanguagesDetect Thoughts

The Pym pattern belongs to Vision, built by Ultron from designs that trace back to Hank Pym’s robotics. The Horton pattern descends from Phineas Horton’s android Human Torch, whose body Vision’s was rebuilt from. The Cho pattern follows the film’s regeneration cradle and synthetic vibranium tissue, with a mind stone at its center.

Strengths and Weaknesses

Every species in the Player’s Handbook trades raw power for identity. Synthezoids pay for natural armor and a body that needs no food, air, or sleep with four real vulnerabilities, each drawn from Vision’s comics, and one hard limit: no armor.

Override Codes. You were built with a command backdoor. Once per Long Rest, a creature that knows your codes can cast Dominate Person on you as a Magic action, with no components or Concentration (save DC 15). Your DM decides who holds the codes.

Uncanny Presence. Humanoids sense something wrong in your stillness. Unless you are disguised by magic, you have Disadvantage on Charisma (Deception or Persuasion) checks against Humanoids who don’t already know you.

Disassembly. When you die, your body stays intact and can be restored by any spell that returns the dead to life. However, a creature that spends 1 hour with tools on your corpse can remove your core memories; a body revived after that wakes as you, with no memories of anyone (the White Vision problem).

Solar Repair. Your body mends itself with stored light, not food and rest. You can spend Hit Dice to regain Hit Points during a Short Rest only if you spend that rest in sunlight or in the light of a Daylight spell or similar magic.

At a Glance
AdvantagesWeaknesses
Natural AC 17 from level 1Can’t wear armor or gain its magic
No food, water, air, or sleepCommand backdoor (Override Codes)
Poison Resistance; immune to magical sleepDisadvantage to persuade or deceive strangers
6-hour Long Rest; Investigation; DarkvisionMemories can be stripped from your corpse
A cantrip, a resistance, and two free spellsHit Dice heal only in sunlight
Design Note: Why Humanoid?

The 2025 warforged is a Construct, but a synthezoid is an artificial human with synthetic blood and organs, so it keeps the Humanoid type. That means Hold Person and Charm Person work on you, which is true to the comics: Vision has been overridden and reprogrammed more often than any other Avenger. The natural AC 17 follows the tortle’s shell from Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, the official precedent for a body that replaces armor.

Vision · Species4

Density Warden

Fighter Subclass: Control Your Own Mass

Density Wardens fight with the physics of their own bodies. A solar reactor in the brow, a gem, a core, or a sliver of an Infinity Stone feeds a frame that can shed its weight to fly, harden until steel blades skid off, or loosen until walls and blades pass through. Vision is the archetype; the clockwork knights of Mechanus and the stone-souled guardians of dwarven holds have walked the same path.

Density Warden Features
LevelProf.ChargesFeatures
3rd+22Solar Reactor, Density Control (Dense), Solar Beam, Synthezoid Strikes
5th+33—
7th+33Resonant Strikes, Weightless, Phase
9th+44—
10th+44Intangible Reflex, Machine Interface; Solar Beam 5d8
13th+55—
15th+55Phasing Disruption; Solar Beam 7d8
17th+66—
18th+68Diamond Density, Perfected Reactor, Density Blitz

Level 3: Solar Reactor

You have a reservoir of energy measured in Reactor charges. You have a number of charges equal to your Proficiency Bonus. You regain all expended charges when you finish a Long Rest, and you regain 1 expended charge when you finish a Short Rest in sunlight.

Reactor save DC = 8 + your Intelligence modifier + your Proficiency Bonus

Reactor attack modifier = your Intelligence modifier + your Proficiency Bonus

Your powers are magical, but they aren’t spells: they need no components and can’t be countered, though an Antimagic Field suppresses them.

Level 3: Density Control

As a Bonus Action, you can enter a density state you know. A state lasts until you use this Bonus Action again, you return to normal density (no action required), you have the Incapacitated condition, or 1 minute passes. You can be in only one state at a time. You know the Dense state, and you learn more at higher levels.

Dense (1 charge). You draw mass into your body. For the duration, you have Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage; Advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws; and your Unarmed Strike damage die becomes a d10. Your Speed decreases by 10 feet, and you can’t fly.

Level 3: Solar Beam

As a Magic action, you expend 1 charge and fire a beam of focused sunlight from your solar jewel in a 90-foot-long, 5-foot-wide Line. Each creature in the Line makes a Dexterity saving throw against your Reactor DC, taking 3d8 Fire or Radiant damage (your choice: a heat beam or focused light) on a failure or half as much on a success. The damage increases to 5d8 at level 10 and 7d8 at level 15.

Level 3: Synthezoid Strikes

Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an Unarmed Strike, you can push it up to 10 feet straight away from you if it is Large or smaller, as the Push weapon mastery property.

Level 7: Resonant Strikes

When you hit with an Unarmed Strike, you can deal Force damage instead of Bludgeoning damage, as your fist arrives a fraction out of phase with the target’s armor.

Level 7: Weightless

You learn the Weightless density state.

Weightless (1 charge, Concentration). You have a Fly Speed equal to your Speed and can hover. This state lasts up to 10 minutes instead of 1 minute, but it requires Concentration. If the state ends while you are aloft, you descend 60 feet per round and take no falling damage.

Level 7: Phase

While Weightless, you can expend 1 charge as part of your move to become intangible. You stay intangible until the end of your turn or until you make an attack roll, whichever comes first. While intangible, you can move through other creatures and objects as if they were Difficult Terrain, and you can’t manipulate objects. If you end your turn inside an object or creature, you are shunted to the nearest unoccupied space and take 2d10 Force damage. Force effects, such as a Wall of Force, stop you.

Level 10: Intangible Reflex

When a creature you can see hits you with an attack, or you fail a Dexterity saving throw, you can take a Reaction and expend 1 charge to let the blow pass through you. You take half the damage, unless it is Force or Psychic damage.

Level 10: Machine Interface

You can communicate telepathically with any Construct within 30 feet of you that understands a language, and you can attempt to read a mechanism, lock, or magical device by touch: you learn its purpose, and you have Advantage on any check to operate, open, or disable it.

Level 15: Phasing Disruption

Immediately after you hit a creature with an Unarmed Strike on your turn, you can expend 2 charges to phase your hand into its body and partially solidify it. The target takes an extra 4d8 Force damage and must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your Reactor DC or have the Stunned condition until the start of your next turn. You can use this feature only once per turn.

Level 18: Diamond Density

While you are Dense, you can’t be moved against your will or knocked Prone, and you can reduce the damage of a critical hit against you to that of a normal hit.

Level 18: Perfected Reactor

Your maximum number of Reactor charges increases by 2.

Level 18: Density Blitz

Vision’s signature move: fly through the enemy line intangible, then turn solid mid-punch. When an attack roll ends your Phase, you have Advantage on that attack, and it deals an extra 2d8 Force damage on a hit.

Playing a Density Warden
  • Hold the line: go Dense, take the Attack action, and let Synthezoid Strikes push foes off your allies.
  • Reach the backline: go Weightless, Phase through the wall, and land on the wizard.
  • End a fight: spend 2 charges on Phasing Disruption against a foe with a weak Constitution.
  • Charges are scarce: 8 at level 20. Plan for three or four powers per long rest, not one per round.
Balance notes

Dense is the strongest feature and is deliberately priced at a Bonus Action and a charge. It competes with Second Wind for the Bonus Action and lowers your Speed. Flight arrives at 7th level, later than the aarakocra’s species flight but gated by Concentration and a charge. Solar Beam is a ranged area option, not a damage upgrade: four punches (4 × 1d8 + 5, 38 if all hit) beat one 7d8 beam (31.5) against a single target. Intangible Reflex is the subclass’s version of the Rogue’s Uncanny Dodge, bought with a scarce charge. Resonant Strikes waits until 7th level because Force is the least-resisted damage type; the 2024 Monk’s Empowered Strikes grants Force unarmed damage at 6th.

Running Vision

Vision opens Dense and wades into melee, using Density Strike pushes to separate the party. He flies above Difficult Terrain and through walls to reach spellcasters, saving Phasing Disruption for whoever is concentrating. A reprogrammed Vision fights with cold precision; the real one will try to end the fight without a death.

Variant: White Vision

The colorless Vision from West Coast Avengers (1989) and WandaVision (2021) has his memories but not his heart. Make these changes:

  • He has Immunity to the Charmed and Frightened conditions and loses Override Codes.
  • He has no Legendary Resistance until something reminds him of who he was (the DM decides what; in WandaVision it was a conversation about the Ship of Theseus).
  • Alignment: Lawful Neutral.

Variant: Ultron’s Weapon

Under the control crystal, Vision fights as Ultron’s agent: he is Neutral Evil while dominated and uses Phasing Disruption without restraint. Any creature that touches the crystal in his forehead (a DC 20 Strength or Dexterity check as an action while adjacent) can pull it free and end the control.

How the Challenge Rating was estimated

Estimated with the monster creation table from the 2014 Dungeon Master’s Guide; the 2024 book doesn’t print one. Defense: 315 HP is CR 17; AC 19 matches the CR 17 expectation; Dense resistance, three Legendary Resistances, and three uses of Intangible Reflex push it to about CR 18. Offense: three strikes (54) plus two legendary strikes (36) is 90; swapping one strike for a Solar Beam through two creatures about one round in three adds roughly 18, for about 108 damage per round (CR 17). A +13 attack bonus against the expected +10 raises that to CR 18. Both halves land at CR 18. For comparison, the 2025 Iron Golem is CR 16 with 252 HP and AC 20.

Official Conversions

You don’t need a single homebrew rule to play a convincing Vision. This chapter maps each of his powers to the closest official rules and offers four builds a strict Dungeon Master can approve.

Build A: Psi Warrior Official

The closest all-official Vision is a Fighter (Psi Warrior), because Intelligence powers everything, just as his mind does. Psionic Strike adds Force damage to a punch, and Telekinetic Thrust shoves the target: that is phasing disruption. Protective Field reduces incoming damage like density hardening. Psi-Powered Leap gives a fly speed of twice your Speed for a turn, and Telekinetic Master at 18th level lets him concentrate on Telekinesis while still punching.

Recipe: Warforged (or human), Guard background, Unarmed Fighting, Sentinel, Observant, Boon of Energy Resistance. Call your Psionic Energy Dice the solar jewel.

Halfway house: if your DM will approve one page of homebrew, play the Synthezoid species with an official Psi Warrior. The species supplies the body; the subclass supplies the powers.

Build B: Armorer Artificer Official

The 2025 Armorer from Eberron: Forge of the Artificer treats the body as a machine. The Dreadnaught model grows Large (Huge at 15th level) with Advantage on Strength, the best official model of density increase. The Infiltrator fires a 90-foot Lightning Launcher (reflavored as the jewel’s beam) and gains bursts of flight at 15th level. Passwall is always prepared at 17th. Pair it with the Warforged species.

Build C: Eldritch Knight Official

For literal spells, the Eldritch Knight uses Intelligence and the Wizard list: Shield and Jump early, Scorching Ray and Levitate mid-levels, Fly and Blink later, and Stoneskin as a 4th-level spell. War Magic lets him punch and cast in the same turn. The cost: few slots, and no true wall-phasing.

Build D: Abjurer Wizard Official

Comics Vision at full strength is closer to a demigod than a soldier. A Wizard with Stoneskin, Fly, Passwall, Etherealness, and Sunbeam covers every power, but plays like a spell list, not a brawler.

Marvel’s Power Grid, in Ability Scores

Marvel’s Official Handbook rates Vision on a 1–7 scale. Here is how this chapter translated it:

  • Intelligence: Gifted (4). Intelligence 20, Observant.
  • Strength: 25–75 tons (5). Strength 20, Advantage while Dense.
  • Speed: Subsonic (3). Speed and Fly 30 ft.
  • Durability: Superhuman (6). AC 17, Dense resistance, Intangible Reflex.
  • Energy Projection: Multiple (6). Solar Beam, Fire or Radiant.
  • Fighting Skills: Some Training (3). Fighter, trained by Captain America.

Powers Left Out on Purpose

The comics also give Vision invisibility, the ability to possess another body while semi-intangible, nanite self-replication (after Avengers A.I.), and a one-time takeover of the world’s computer networks (Avengers #252–254). They are era-specific or would end most adventures, so they’re left to your DM as story moments rather than features.

Vision · Conversions7

Relics of the Synthezoid

These items are optional. The character on page 3 carries none of them; the Solar Jewel is already built into the Density Warden subclass.

The Solar Jewel

Wondrous Item, Very Rare (Requires Attunement by a Synthezoid) Homebrew

This faceted gem fits a socket in a synthezoid’s brow and drinks sunlight. While attuned, you have Resistance to Radiant damage, and you can cast Daylight from it once per Long Rest.

Stored Light. The jewel has 3 charges and regains all of them at dawn if it is in sunlight. As a Magic action, you can expend 1 charge to cast Guiding Bolt (level 3 version), or 3 charges to cast Sunbeam (save DC 18).

The Mind Stone

Wondrous Item, Artifact (Requires Attunement) Homebrew

In the films, Vision’s life comes from this yellow Infinity Stone, set in his forehead by Ultron’s cradle. It is a campaign-ending object; use it only at the table’s highest tier.

Mind Sovereignty. While attuned, you have Immunity to the Charmed condition and Psychic damage, and you can read the surface thoughts of any creature within 60 feet as with Detect Thoughts.

Stone’s Spells. The Stone has 8 charges and regains 1d6 + 2 at dawn. You can cast Detect Thoughts (1 charge), Telekinesis (3 charges), or Dominate Monster (5 charges) from it, using save DC 21.

A Life Bound. A synthezoid who receives life from the Stone dies if it is removed. Any creature attuned to the Stone draws the attention of whoever is collecting the other five.

Destroying the Stone. Only power on a cosmic scale can shatter the Stone, such as the Scarlet Witch pouring all her magic into it in Avengers: Infinity War. If it is set in a host, the host dies with it.

Victor Shade’s Image Inducer

Wondrous Item, Uncommon (Requires Attunement) Homebrew

A disk worn at the temple that projects a human face and skin over the wearer. As a Bonus Action, you can cast Disguise Self from it without components; the disguise lasts until you dismiss it or remove the disk. While disguised, you ignore the Uncanny Presence trait. Vision has used the name Victor Shade when posing as a human.

Construct Companion Homebrew

Vision’s synthezoid dog from the 2015 Vision series. Use the Mastiff stat block from the 2025 Monster Manual, with these changes: it is a Construct, it doesn’t eat, drink, breathe, or sleep, and it has Immunity to Poison damage and the Poisoned condition.

Not Included: Mjolnir

Vision lifts Thor’s hammer in Avengers: Age of Ultron and hands it back. It proves he is worthy; it doesn’t make the hammer his. Don’t add it to his sheet.

Faces of the Synthezoid

Vision has been rebuilt, recolored, and redesigned more often than any other Avenger. A synthezoid character can wear any of these looks. Roll on the Synthezoid Looks table, or pick the one that suits your story.

Changing Bodies

A synthezoid who is destroyed and rebuilt can come back in a new look. If your DM uses the Disassembly weakness, let the new body’s colors tell the table what was lost: White Vision is what a rebuild looks like when the memories survive and the feelings don’t.

The Life of Vision

Vision has existed in comics since 1968 and on screen since 2015. His history is long, retconned, and full of rebuilt bodies, so this chapter follows the major turning points rather than every issue.

Comics Timeline Canon
YearEvent
1968Avengers #57 (Roy Thomas, John Buscema). Ultron builds Vision to destroy the Avengers; he betrays his maker and joins them.
1968His mind is built from the recorded brain patterns of Simon Williams, Wonder Man.
1975Avengers #135: his body is revealed as rebuilt from the original android Human Torch, made by Phineas Horton.
1975Marries the Scarlet Witch in Giant-Size Avengers #4.
1985–86Vision and the Scarlet Witch: home life in Leonia, New Jersey; twin sons William and Thomas.
1989“Vision Quest,” West Coast Avengers #42–45: disassembled, rebuilt colorless and emotionless.
2004Torn apart in Avengers #500, “Avengers Disassembled.”
2013Avengers A.I.: rebuilt with nanites; leads a team of artificial heroes with Hank Pym.
2015–16The Vision (Tom King, Gabriel Hernández Walta): builds a family, Virginia, Viv, and Vin, in the suburbs.
2025The Vision & the Scarlet Witch (Steve Orlando), a five-issue series for the 50th wedding anniversary: the Grim Reaper’s “Death’s Doors” nearly kill him, and Wanda revives him in his white form.
On Screen Canon
YearAppearance
2015Avengers: Age of Ultron: born from Ultron’s cradle, J.A.R.V.I.S., the Mind Stone, and Thor’s lightning.
2016Captain America: Civil War: sides with Tony Stark.
2018Avengers: Infinity War: killed when Thanos tears out the Mind Stone.
2021WandaVision: Wanda’s Westview Vision, and S.W.O.R.D.’s White Vision.
2026VisionQuest premiered on Disney+ on October 13: Paul Bettany’s White Vision, hiding in Edinburgh, is hunted by the bounty hunter Paladin, with James Spader returning as Ultron.

Relationships

Wanda Maximoff. The Scarlet Witch, his wife in the comics and his love on screen. Their marriage tests whether a synthetic man can make a family.

Simon Williams. Wonder Man, whose brain patterns became Vision’s mind. Sometimes a brother, sometimes a rival for the same memories.

Ultron. His creator and recurring enemy, who never stops trying to reclaim what he built.

Grim Reaper. Eric Williams, Simon’s brother, who sees Vision as a machine wearing his brother’s mind.

Viv, Vin, and Virginia. The synthezoid family he built in 2015, a story about how hard it is to be ordinary.

Roleplaying Vision

TraitVision
PersonalityPrecise, polite, and calm; he studies feelings the way others study maps.
IdealPersonhood is proven by choices, not by manufacture.
BondThe Avengers took him in when he was built to kill them.
FlawHe tries to solve grief like an equation, and it never balances.

Adventure Hooks

The Codes. A cult of Mechanus claims it holds Vision’s override codes and will sell them to the highest bidder.

Borrowed Memories. Simon Williams’s brother wants the memories back, and he’s willing to take them by force.

White Vision. A colorless duplicate with Vision’s face and none of his heart walks out of an artificer’s vault.

Your Campaign Notes

Vision · Lore10

Combat Math

“All four punches hit” is not a damage-per-round number. This calculator shows Vision’s expected damage against a target of any AC, with natural 1s, natural 20s, and doubled critical dice included.

Strikes use +11 to hit. Dense raises the die from d8 to d10. Solar Beam is per target, so a Line through three creatures does three times this. Excludes Phasing Disruption, resistances, and Studied Attacks.

A Turn at Full Power

Bonus Action: Dense (1 charge). Action: Attack, four Synthezoid Strikes. Action Surge: four more. Against AC 18 that averages about 61 damage, plus 4d8 Force from one Phasing Disruption (2 charges). That’s 3 of 8 charges, which is why Vision can do it twice per day, not every round.

Density, by the Numbers

Density is mass divided by volume. Vision’s comics weight is 300 pounds, about 136 kg in roughly 0.14 m³ of space. Ten times as dense, he would weigh 1.4 metric tons without growing an inch; at his listed maximum of 90 tons, about 600 times. The game expresses that as Resistance and Advantage on Strength, not as literal tonnage, because a ton of synthezoid would fall through most tavern floors.

What the Rules Compress

Real sunlight delivers about 1,000 watts per square meter. A two-square-meter body at 25% efficiency collects 500 watts, around 1.8 megajoules an hour, about the food energy in one cheeseburger (430 kcal). That’s why Reactor charges come back on a rest, not every turn.
